originalTitle: The studio behind Pokémon struggles to find its voice in Beast of Reincarnation

content: You have to imagine that the team at Game Freak is bursting with ideas. The studio puts out new mainline Pokémon adventures with a machinelike precision. But every so often it launches a curious experiment, whether it’s an action title about a militarized elephant or turning horse races into a card game, showing that it’s capable of more than the latest generation of pocket monsters. That’s part of what makes the idea of Beast of Reincarnation so enticing. Here is an established studio breaking free of the franchise it has become known for to make its take on a blockbuster action game. Unfortunately new ideas are in short supply in Beast, and aside from its slick action, there’s little that hasn’t been done before. Beast of Reincarnation takes place exactly 2,000 years in the future in a postapocalyptic vision of Japan that blends sci-fi and magic. Humans still exist, though many of them transferred their consciousness to robotic golems in order to survive the calamity that ruined the world. The real problem is that a mysterious blight has infected the landscape, turning wildlife into vicious, mutated monsters. Even worse: This seems to portend the return of the titular beast, a powerful creature that, as its name implies, appears to be immortal. You play as a wandering mercenary-type named Emma who has the ability to absorb the powers of fallen mutants, and soon she’s tasked with traversing the world to power up so that she can take down the beast for good. It’s not a bad setup for an action game, as it gives you a reason to keep moving forward. Emma is constantly on the hunt for the next big creature that she can use to get stronger before taking on her final task. Beast of Reincarnation isn’t an open-world game, but instead is divided into a series of big locations that you travel between as the story progresses. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/BoR-Screenshot-20.png?quality=90&strip=all] The standout feature of the game is its action. Emma is a speedy samurai type, wielding a blade and various bows. At first, Beast seems like Dark Souls or Elden Ring, a game built around dodging and parrying, with little room for error. But as you unlock new powers, it proves to be something a little different. Emma’s signature ability is that vines and plants can grow out of her hair. This sounds weird, but it’s also incredibly useful; she can build bridges to traverse big gaps, or use her hair like a grappling hook to reach locations up high. She also has an adorable and gigantic magical dog companion who follows her everywhere and provides a hand with combat and tedious chores like collecting loot. Emma’s powers are especially helpful in battle. Slowly she gains abilities that let her zip around the battlefield, using her hair to quickly gain ground on an enemy, deliver an attack from above, or team up with her powerful pup for a devastating blow. Her hair can even improve your stealth: At one point I unlocked a skill that caused tall plants to sprout wherever I crouched, temporarily giving me some cover before delivering a silent kill. It takes a few hours for things to open up, but eventually Beast’s combat has plenty of room for freedom and creativity. The same can’t be said for the rest of the experience. Initially, Beast’s postapocalyptic world is compelling because it’s full of mystery. You know almost nothing about the history of the world, but there are hints of interesting dynamics, like the human-infused machines and how they evolved differently from flesh-and-blood people. But Beast pushes the idea of mystery to a frustrating extreme. Everything in this game is mysterious: the landscape, Emma herself, her two human travel companions, her giant dog, the little girl that only Emma can see, the other wandering fighters she encounters in the world. I love a story that is full of secrets and intrigue, but I barely understood what I was even doing in Beast until at least a dozen hours into the game. It doesn’t help that the game hides explanations of many of its key elements in a tutorial menu. And when you do finally get answers to the big mysteries, they’re mostly underwhelming. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/BoR-Screenshot-9.png?quality=90&strip=all] The story isn’t the only place that feels underdeveloped or uninspired. There are a number of gameplay elements — like the ability to grow your own food, and a weapon upgrade system — that are so simple that it’s easy to forget about them altogether. Meanwhile, the level design is incredibly straightforward, making exploration a bore, particularly when it comes to the dead-simple platforming sections. The game’s skill tree is even a literal tree. But the real issue with Beast of Reincarnation is that it is full of ideas that already exist elsewhere. The story is like a watered-down version of Nier: Automata’s heartrending postapocalypse, while the boss battles feel ripped out of Monster Hunter (with designs straight from its contemporary Wild Hearts and one specific creature that looks identical to a Stranger Things demodog). Your mobile home base functions much like the one in Death Stranding — you can even shower — and it looks just like an AT-ST from Star Wars. Everywhere you go, there’s something from a different game or movie. This is especially disappointing because there is so much potential in Beast of Reincarnation. Not only is the combat thrilling, but, as derivative as it is, the game still manages to create an incredible sense of melancholic moodiness through its sound and visuals. But it never delivers on that; I was excited to learn about the strange religions and customs that were developed by isolated groups of golem, for instance, but the revelations were all surface level and quickly brushed aside. chineseTitle: 神奇宝贝背后的工作室努力在《轮回之兽》中找到自己的声音

chineseContent: 你必须想象 Game Freak 的团队充满了创意。该工作室以机器般的精度推出了新的主线神奇宝贝冒险游戏。但它时不时地会推出一项奇怪的实验，无论是关于军事化大象的动作游戏，还是将赛马变成纸牌游戏，都表明它的能力不仅仅是最新一代的口袋妖怪。这就是《轮回之兽》的想法如此诱人的部分原因。这是一家成熟的工作室，摆脱了其因制作热门动作游戏而闻名的特许经营权。不幸的是，《野兽》中的新想法供不应求，除了其灵活的动作之外，几乎没有什么是以前没有做过的。 《转生之兽》的故事发生在 2000 年后的未来，融合了科幻和魔法的日本后世界末日景象。人类仍然存在，尽管他们中的许多人将自己的意识转移到机器人傀儡上，以便在毁灭世界的灾难中生存下来。真正的问题是一种神秘的枯萎病已经感染了这片土地，将野生动物变成了邪恶的变异怪物。更糟糕的是：这似乎预示着名义上的野兽的回归，这是一种强大的生物，正如它的名字所暗示的那样，它似乎是不朽的。你扮演一个名叫艾玛的流浪雇佣兵，她有能力吸收堕落变种人的力量，很快她的任务就是穿越世界来增强力量，这样她就可以永远消灭这只野兽。对于动作游戏来说，这并不是一个糟糕的设置，因为它给了你继续前进的理由。艾玛一直在寻找下一个大型生物，在完成最后的任务之前，她可以利用它来变得更强。 《轮回之兽》不是一款开放世界游戏，而是分为一系列大地点
